subtopics.title: The Plane, the Points, and the Distance Formula

questions.question: The distance formula is really an application of:
For A(−3; 2) and B(5; 8), the horizontal difference is:
The length of AB for A(−3; 2) and B(5; 8) is:
Why does swapping the order of the two points leave the distance unchanged?
options: Because distance is always a whole number
Because the formula uses only the first point
Because the coordinates are added, not subtracted
Because each difference is squared, and squaring destroys the sign

questions.question: The midpoint of the segment joining A(−3; 2) and B(5; 8) is:
Which of the three formulae ADDS the coordinates rather than subtracting them?
M(1; 5) is the midpoint of AB and A is (−3; 2). The coordinates of B are:
To prove that the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, you show that:
options: The diagonals are equal in length
Both diagonals have the SAME midpoint

questions.question: The gradient of the line through A(−3; 2) and B(5; 8) is:
The gradient of a VERTICAL line is:
options: Undefined, because the change in x is zero and you cannot divide by zero

questions.question: A line has gradient 3/4. A line perpendicular to it has gradient:
P(1; 2), Q(3; 6) and R(5; 10) are shown to be collinear because:
options: The midpoint of PR is Q
Gradient PQ = gradient QR = 2, and the lines share the point Q

questions.question: For A(−3; 2), B(5; 8), C(9; 3) and D(1; −3), the lengths AB and CD are both:
The diagonals AC and BD of that quadrilateral both have midpoint:
Gradient AB × gradient AD = 3/4 × (−5/4) = −15/16. This shows that ABCD is:
options: NOT a rectangle, because the product is not −1, so angle A is not a right angle

questions.question: Which conclusion about ABCD is fully justified by the calculations?
options: It is a rectangle, because it looks like one
It is a rhombus, because AB = CD
It is a parallelogram and nothing more — opposite sides equal and parallel, diagonals bisecting, but no right angle and no four equal sides

subtopics.title: Eight Blocks Across, Six Blocks Up

questions.question: Eight blocks east and six blocks north. Walking the streets is 14 blocks. Cutting straight across the field is:
The three moves of the distance recipe are:
options: Add across and up, then halve
Find how far across, find how far up, then square both, add, and take the square root

questions.question: Why can a distance never come out negative?
options: Because you always subtract the smaller from the larger
Because squaring wipes out any minus sign before the square root is taken

questions.question: Two friends live at house numbers 3 and 11. They meet at house number:
The memory rule separating the three formulae is:
options: Middle means ADD and halve; steepness and distance mean SUBTRACT
Middle means subtract; distance means add
Steepness means add; middle means multiply

questions.question: Your midpoint answer lands OUTSIDE the two given points. The most likely cause is:
options: The points were in the wrong order
You subtracted where you should have added
You forgot to take a square root
The two points are too far apart

questions.question: Two roads cross, and each is cut exactly in half at the crossing. On a grid this shows up as:
options: Equal lengths for the two roads
Both roads having the SAME midpoint

subtopics.title: Steepness You Can Feel — and the Traps

questions.question: A gradient of 3/4 means:
options: The line drops 3 for every 4 across
The line is 3/4 of a unit long
For every 4 units across, the line climbs 3 units up
The line makes an angle of 34 degrees

questions.question: A soccer field is flat and a wall is straight up. Their gradients are:
options: Zero for the wall, undefined for the field
Zero for the field, undefined for the wall

questions.question: What is your proof of a right angle on a grid?
options: The two gradients multiply to give −1
The two sides are equal in length
The corner looks square in the sketch

questions.question: A learner computes a gradient using the second point's y on top but the first point's x underneath. The result will be:
options: Correct, since order does not matter for gradient
Wrong — mixing the order flips the sign, turning a rising line into a falling one
Correct, but only for positive coordinates
